title: Surgical atrial fibrillation and Maze procedure: biophysics, Cox-Maze IV lesion set, appendage exclusion and LAAOS III
subject: ss-ctvs

2017 STS Clinical Practice Guideline on the Surgical Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation
2020 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of atrial fibrillation

steps.say: The surgical Maze procedure eliminates atrial fibrillation by interrupting reentry circuits. Full-thickness ablation lines create permanent electrical conduction block, compartmentalizing the atria so macro-reentrant wavelets cannot propagate. This restores sinus rhythm and preserves coordinated atrioventricular mechanical transport.
steps.tx: The surgical **Maze procedure** permanently eliminates atrial fibrillation by creating transmural lines of electrical **conduction block**. These deliberate barriers compartmentalize the atria, disrupting **macro-reentrant wavelets** while allowing normal sinus node impulses to depolarize the atria and preserve physiological atrioventricular mechanical transport.

steps.say: The modern Cox-Maze IV procedure replaces historical surgical incisions with advanced energy devices. Bipolar radiofrequency clamps and cryoablation probes create transmural lesions rapidly and safely without cutting atrial tissue. Real-time electrical conductance feedback confirms complete transmurality before clamp release.
steps.tx: The contemporary **Cox-Maze IV** procedure replaces historical cut-and-sew incisions with **bipolar radiofrequency** energy and **cryoablation** tools. Bipolar clamps compress atrial tissue and measure electrical impedance in real time, delivering uniform, full-thickness transmural lesions that duplicate the efficacy of traditional incisions in minutes, completing version 4 of the procedure.

left.title: Cox-Maze IV Technique
points: Significantly shorter cross-clamp and bypass times
Minimal bleeding risk with verified transmurality

right.title: Historical Cox-Maze III
points: Multiple surgical incisions and extensive suture lines
Prolonged cardiopulmonary bypass and arrest times
High risk of postoperative bleeding and reoperation

steps.say: The Cox-Maze IV lesion set isolates the posterior left atrium and pulmonary veins. It includes bilateral pulmonary vein isolation, connecting roof and floor lines creating a posterior box lesion, and a mitral isthmus line extending to the annulus. Right atrial ablation lines are added for a biatrial Maze.
steps.tx: The standard Cox-Maze 4 lesion set encompasses bilateral **pulmonary vein isolation**, roof and floor lines forming a posterior left atrial **box lesion**, and a **mitral isthmus line** extending across the coronary sinus to the mitral valve annulus, alongside complementary right atrial lines during full biatrial procedures.

nodes.label: Encircle left and right pulmonary veins with bipolar clamp
Construct connecting roof and floor lines to form posterior box
Ablate mitral isthmus to annulus with bipolar clamp and cryoprobe
Perform right atrial lesions down to tricuspid annulus

steps.say: Cryoablation is essential for ablating the mitral isthmus and coronary sinus safely. Applying cryoablation temperatures down to negative sixty degrees Celsius for two minutes freezes tissue through its full thickness. Unlike radiofrequency heat, freezing preserves collagen architecture and protects the adjacent circumflex coronary artery.
steps.tx: Surgical **cryoablation temperature** reaches -60 degrees Celsius for 2 minutes to ablate the thick muscular **mitral isthmus** and adjacent **coronary sinus**. Cryotherapy preserves collagen scaffolding and avoids thermal tissue vaporization, eliminating the catastrophic hazard of circumflex coronary artery thrombosis during deep myocardial freezing.

rows: Protects vessel collagen matrix; safe near circumflex artery
Resistive heating and cellular coagulative necrosis
Strictly clamped across folded tissue; avoids thermal spread
Conductive thermal heating into blood pool
High risk of collateral tissue injury; avoided near vessels

steps.say: Guidelines give a Class I recommendation for concomitant surgical ablation during mitral valve surgery. Restoring sinus rhythm dramatically improves long-term survival, reduces stroke risk, and enhances functional exercise capacity. Over seventy to eighty percent of patients maintain stable sinus rhythm at one year.
steps.tx: A **Class I recommendation** governs **concomitant ablation** during indicated mitral valve surgery. Restoring normal **sinus rhythm restoration** occurs in over 70 to 80 percent of patients at 1 year postoperatively, significantly lowering long-term heart failure hospitalizations and stroke without increasing baseline operative mortality.

nodes.label: Patient with AF undergoing mitral valve surgery
Evaluate left atrial size and duration of arrhythmia
Perform concomitant Cox-Maze IV ablation procedure
Achieve > 70-80% sinus rhythm maintenance at 1 year

steps.say: The left atrial appendage is the main source of intracardiac thrombus. It accounts for over ninety percent of thrombi in non-valvular atrial fibrillation and over fifty percent in rheumatic mitral disease. Stagnant blood flow in the trabeculated appendage promotes rapid clot formation during fibrillation.
steps.tx: The **left atrial appendage** is the dominant intracardiac **thrombus source**, responsible for over 90 percent of left atrial thrombi in non-valvular atrial fibrillation and over 50 percent in rheumatic mitral valve stenosis. Mechanical stasis within its trabeculated pectinate muscles drives catastrophic **thromboembolism**.

left.title: Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation
points: Over 90% of cardiogenic thrombi arise within the appendage
Trabeculated pectinate pockets create severe stasis
Appendage occlusion dramatically reduces embolic stroke

right.title: Rheumatic Mitral Disease
points: Over 50% of thrombi originate in left atrial appendage
Substantial thrombus also forms on enlarged atrial body wall
Requires both appendage exclusion and atrial cavity debridement

steps.say: Complete left atrial appendage exclusion prevents thromboembolic stroke. Epicardial clip devices like the AtriClip achieve reliable electrical and mechanical exclusion without entering the atrial cavity. The operator must position the clip at the true anatomical base to avoid leaving a residual stump larger than one centimetre.
steps.tx: Surgical **appendage exclusion** is achieved using external epicardial clips such as the **AtriClip**, surgical staplers, or internal continuous suture lines. Perfect exclusion at the true anatomical base is vital, ensuring no persistent **residual stump** larger than 1 cm remains to harbor stagnant blood.

rows: Bipolar clip with polyester knit covering
Zero foreign body inside atrium; electrical isolation
Performed from within atrium during open mitral surgery

steps.say: The landmark LAAOS III trial confirmed the profound benefits of surgical appendage occlusion. In patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing cardiac surgery, adding appendage occlusion reduced the three-year risk of ischemic stroke and systemic embolism by thirty-three percent. This trial established appendage closure as a cornerstone of cardiac surgery.
steps.tx: The randomized **LAAOS III trial** demonstrated that surgical left atrial appendage occlusion during routine cardiac surgery in patients with atrial fibrillation achieves a 33 percent **stroke reduction** at 3 years. This protective effect against **ischemic embolism** persisted independently of continued postoperative oral anticoagulation therapy.
